criteria.note:
What works:
- Seven real slides. One touch swipe moves exactly one slide (1→2→3→2 / 7), loads that slide and its neighbour, and announces '2 of 7'.
- A vertical drag that starts on the photo scrolls the page (to scrollY 294).
- Each slide is a named group.
- Tapping a photo opens the viewer with Shopify's 1200w originals.
- The viewer now pages with the arrow keys and announces the position, and Escape returns focus to #track.
- Size guide opens the ruler in the viewer where she reads the specs (size_viewer.png).
- A Riya landing opens on 5 / 7, fetches only riya-540, hides the chip and reads 'From Riya's reel'.

Remaining:
- The viewer has no zoom of its own; it relies on the browser's pinch. A synthesized pinch did not change visualViewport.scale in headless, so this is unverified.
- The originals are 896x1200, which is a 1.3x upscale for a 390 px DPR 3 screen (needs input).

What works:
- No MP4 bytes load before a tap; a tap makes one 142 KB request.
- The viewer shows 'Creator collaboration · Riya', and the plate, the chip and both tiles name the clip by their content.
- The clip plays once with sound, then loops muted.
- The clip's burned captions ('and this bracelet is the one', 'people stop you for') satisfy WCAG 1.2.2 as open captions.

Remaining: the source is 270x480 drawn at 360x640, so it is soft, and those captions render about 10 px tall (clip_strip.jpg). Only a clean edit from the 4K F67 timeline fixes either (roadmap).

axe-core (wcag2a/aa, 21aa, 22aa, best-practice) finds 0 violations in all 9 states: load, the card, the one-piece bag, the bag with the policy open, the two-piece bag, the hand-off, after a set add, the clip in the viewer, and all folds open (ax6.json).

Contrast (computed, alpha composited, contrast6.js): no failure; the lowest is 4.84:1 (deep sage on ivory). Ivory on deep sage in the footer is also 4.84:1.

Type and targets:
- Every interactive target is at least 44 px.
- Sizes in use: 11/12/13/15/18/20/24/27 px; nothing under 11.
- lang en-IN, one H1, ordered H2s, and a polite status region outside main.
- inert under the overlays, with Tab trapped in the bag and the viewer.
- Focus returns to the opener after the bag (bagbtn), the viewer (tosize) and the hand-off.

Remaining:
(1) Focus after scripted jumps (tapfocus.js, bagpol6.js). After Read the policy and Back, the page is at 395 but focus stays on the fold's summary 2,600 px below. After the card's 'See the whole set' focus falls to BODY. A screen-reader user loses her place both times (WCAG 2.4.3).
(2) Spacing: the Reviews links and the footer links wrap into rows that touch (0 px apart), and sit 6 px apart side by side. The rubric asks for 8 px between neighbours.

What holds:
- A buy control is on screen at every scroll position; the footer pads for the bar, and at the page end the links end 40 px above it (end_360.png).
- The folds open in place.
- Back closes the bag, the viewer and the hand-off and keeps the scroll (bag at 400 → 400).
- Back undoes every scripted jump, and Back from a set piece's page returns to the set (739 → 739).
- Nothing needed to decide is only in a fold.
- The page is 3,218 px to the footer, 6.5 screens of 498 px. Sections start at: the set 824, Up close 1548, specs 1980, Riya 2401, Reviews 2788, folds 3010.

New fault: the bag's 'Faulty piece? … Read the policy' disclosure opens under the bag's fixed foot. In a one-piece bag at 360x640, 12 of the paragraph's 117 px are visible and the first line is cut by the foot. At 390x664, 36 of 98 px show (bagpol_prototype_360.png). The only visible change is that 'Read the policy' disappears, so the tap reads as dead at the commit point. Fix 1 shows the whole paragraph (117/117 and 98/98).

Lab, 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps, 4x CPU, Android fallback faces (perf.json):
- 360x640: LCP 1.22/1.24 s at DPR 2 and 1.22 s at DPR 3 on worn-720.jpg. FCP 0.38-0.42 s, CLS 0.0001.
- Before scroll at 360x640: 4 image requests plus 2 inline data URIs, 155 KB of images, 351 KB in all (124 KB is the uncompressed document with the notes). Fonts are 71 KB and land at 2.2-2.5 s.
- No video bytes, and the Riya tiles are not fetched before scroll.
- A Riya landing reaches LCP at 0.88 s with 121 KB of images.

Regression from round 5: on screens 2:1 and taller the hero is worn-full-896.jpg, 172 KB at about q90 (all quant steps 5). At 390x844 DPR 3 and 412x915, LCP is 1.80/1.81 s with 254 KB of images, up from about 1.22 s. It is still under the 2.0 s threshold, but now 0.2 s from it. As WebP (79 KB) with a typed preload it drops to 1.28 s with 160 KB (perf_variant.json, fix 3).

Real in-app viewports rarely reach 2:1: Instagram on a 390x844 iPhone is about 390x664. So the cost lands mostly on full-height Safari and Chrome. These are lab figures on a static file; field data is in the roadmap.

With default text, the card never covers the H1, price, ladder or delivery line at any scroll position from 0 to 400, nor at 115% or 130% (docksweep.js). The modes run full → compact → slim → mini → dock. 'none' is used where only the facts are left under it: 220-260 at default, and 60-380 at 130%. Then the bar's '✓ Added to bag' holds for 1.5 s and the badge and the live region confirm the add.

A raw double tap on Add to bag gives one item, with no drawer and no card swap. A double tap on 'Bag & checkout' opens the bag and swallows the checkout tap (guarded: add, checkout), with 0 InitiateCheckout events.

The next step is the bag, and its policy disclosure is the fault under C15.

fixes.where: The drawer's toggle listener, L996. Live: CartDrawerNext, the BagReturns replacement (build note 2).
fixes.change:
When the bag's policy disclosure opens, scroll the bag body just enough to show what it opened:
drawer.addEventListener('toggle', function (ev) { if (ev.target.id === 'drpol' && ev.target.open) { track('nf_bag_policy', { q: stat(bag).q }); var bd = $('#drbody'), over = ev.target.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - bd.getBoundingClientRect().bottom; if (over > 0) bd.scrollBy({ top: over + 4, behavior: smooth() }); } }, true);
The summary stays in view: at 360x640 it moves from 462 to 343. Secure checkout and the COD line do not move.

Measured on variant6 (bagpol6.js, cmp_bagpol.jpg), the opened paragraph is fully visible: 117 of 117 px at 360x640 (was 12) and 98 of 98 at 390x664 (was 36).

In the live bag test, assert that after opening, the paragraph's bottom is at or above the foot's top at 360x640 with one piece.
fixes.why: C15 (a disclosure must show what it opens) and C2's no-half-cut rule, inside the bag. Today the tap leaves one half-cut line under the foot and otherwise looks dead. It sits on the add-to-checkout step that loses 80% of adds, and it is the one place the policy is read at the commit point [N funnel]. Evidence: out/bagpol_prototype_360.png and out/cmp_bagpol.jpg.

fixes.where: The tight-mode script after #product-facts (L512-516), the CSS after L113, and barH() at L1152. Live: PdpBuyFacts and the first-screen budget test (build note 5).
fixes.why: C1 and C2. The column subtracts the inset and the real bar, but tight mode does not, so on any phone with a bottom inset (iPhone Safari, Android 15 edge-to-edge) larger text puts COD under the bar while the remedy stays off. At 150% the fact line is half-cut, and the 180 px band crops the bracelet out of its own hero. Evidence: out/folds_prototype.json against out/folds_variant6.json.

fixes.where: The head script's pre() and the worn picture (L35-47, L455). Live: build note 5 (Shopify p1 at width=900).
fixes.change:
Serve the tall 3:4 frame as WebP, with a typed preload and the JPEG kept as the fallback.
- pre(srcset, media, type) sets l.type = type when given.
- The tall preload becomes pre('i/worn-full-896.webp 896w', '(max-aspect-ratio: 1/2)', 'image/webp').
- The picture gets <source media="(max-aspect-ratio: 1/2)" type="image/webp" data-srcset="i/worn-full-896.webp 896w"> before the existing JPEG source.
The WebP is the same Shopify p1 pixels (896x1200, q75): 79 KB against 172 KB.

Measured on variant6 (perf_variant.json), LCP is 1.28 s at 390x844 DPR 3 and 1.29 s at 412x915 (was 1.80/1.81 s), with images before scroll at 160 KB (was 254). 360x640 is unchanged (1.21 s).

Live: request p1 from the Shopify CDN at width=900, which negotiates WebP or AVIF. Add a perf budget for 390x844 at DPR 3: a landing frame of 90 KB or less and LCP within 0.15 s of 360x640.
fixes.why: C16, a regression from round 5. The tall-screen hero is a q90 JPEG that more than doubles the landing frame and adds about 0.58 s of lab LCP on 2:1 screens, leaving 0.2 s of the 2.0 s budget. Evidence: out/perf.json (p390x844d3 1800 ms; p360d2 1220 ms) and out/perf_variant.json.

fixes.where: The card's data-toset branch L887, the #topolicy handler L1126, and the popstate handler L1096.
fixes.change:
Focus follows every scripted jump and comes back with Back.
- Declare jumpFrom = null beside card/cardY.
- data-toset: after the scrollIntoView, call jumpFrom = addBtn; var sh = $('#set-h'); sh.tabIndex = -1; sh.focus({ preventScroll: true });
- #topolicy: set jumpFrom = this before pushState.
- popstate: if (!layer) { if (jumpFrom) { var jf = jumpFrom; jumpFrom = null; jf.focus({ preventScroll: true }); } return; }

Measured on variant6 (bagpol6.js):
- See the set: focus is on set-h at 133 (was BODY), and Back puts it on #add (was BODY).
- Read the policy and Back: focus returns to #topolicy at 297 (was the fold's summary at 2722).
axe is unchanged (0 violations).
fixes.why: C14 (WCAG 2.4.3 focus order). After Back, a screen-reader or keyboard user's next step starts 2,600 px from what she sees. After the set jump she hears nothing about where she landed. Evidence: out/hist6.json and tapfocus.js.

C14: the rubric asks for at least 8 px between neighbouring targets. Today the footer and Reviews links touch in stacked rows, so a thumb aimed at 'Privacy' can land on 'Contact & business address'. Evidence: out/ax6.json census.close, and out/end_360.png.

fixes.where: The fact line (L505); the bar's label markup in the HTML (L521) and in render() (L760-767); the bag's Secure checkout label (L971).
fixes.change: Keep each separator with what follows it, so a wrapped line never ends on a dangling '·'. - Fact line: Free insured delivery, est. 18–20 Nov · COD available - Bar: Add to bag·₹2,399, with .btn .dot { margin-right: 8px; }. Use the same markup for 'Bag & checkout · ₹X' and 'Secure checkout · ₹X'. At the default size nothing moves. At 115-150% the line breaks as '…18–20 Nov' / '· COD available' and 'ADD TO BAG' / '· ₹2,399', instead of '…18–20 Nov ·' / 'COD available' and 'ADD TO BAG ·' / '₹2,399'. Not built into the variant.
fixes.why: C1 and C14: every larger-text first screen in cmp_r6_largetext.jpg ends its fact line and its primary button on a lone separator, which reads as a cut. The fix costs no height.

keep: The first-screen column: min-height = visible page − header − live --bar − bottom inset − 13 px. The facts take what they need and the photo the rest (180 px floor, 125vw/520 px cap, 133.4vw/560 px on 2:1 screens). The facts end 13 px clear of the bar on every default viewport, with nothing half-cut and no overlap.
html scroll-padding-top and scroll-padding-bottom: no Tab stop is ever hidden behind the bar or the header.

Overlays and jumps own history entries. Scroll restoration is manual only while an overlay is open. Android Back closes the bag, the viewer and the hand-off, and undoes Read the policy and See the set. Back from a set piece's page returns to the set.
inert on header, main and footer under every overlay; Tab trapped in the bag and the viewer; focus returned to the opener.
The viewer: arrow keys page it with announcements, Size guide opens the ruler in place, and Escape returns focus to the gallery.

The landing frame alone is preloaded with fetchpriority=high. Fonts and below-the-fold images are released after the hero (1.2 s cap), with a 451-byte inline placeholder, the chip in the first paint and the bar's first state in the HTML.
Lab LCP of 1.22 s at 360x640 at DPR 2 and 3 with CLS 0.0001, 155 KB of images before scroll, and zero video bytes before a tap.
The 700 ms tap guards on Add to bag, the set rows, the card and the bag's checkout. A double tap never skips the COD figure into Fastrr.
The card never covers the H1, price, ladder or delivery line at any scroll position or text size tested, and the dock tests #product-facts.
axe-clean in 9 states; computed contrast at 4.84:1 or above everywhere; every target at least 44 px; an 11 px floor; lang en-IN; a polite status region outside main.
The bar's ResizeObserver: at 150-200% text the buttons grow instead of clipping 'Add to bag'.
The footer's green ends 12 px above the bar's hairline, so the bar never sits over footer text.
roadmap: Field data from the Instagram webview: web-vitals LCP, INP and CLS sent with naira_vid and the arm to the meta-capi/Supabase path, split by viewport class (360x640, 390x664, 2:1). This replaces lab-only C16 scoring and shows how often the 2:1 picture source actually matches inside the in-app browser.
Check whether Instagram's Android WebView applies the system Font size (WebSettings.textZoom), on one Android 14 phone at 130% and 200%. The 150-200% budget matters only if it does.
Measure env(safe-area-inset-bottom) in the field on Android 15 edge-to-edge devices, in the Instagram webview and in Chrome. Log it once per session as a Clarity tag.
Shopify originals at least 1,440 px wide, for DPR 3 sharpness, then in-viewer double-tap zoom to 2x on the original (transform-based, so the page zoom never sticks after Back).

A clean Riya edit cut from the 4K F67 timeline at 720x1280, under 1 MB, with the captions as a WebVTT track at a readable size instead of today's burned 10 px captions, plus a 6-10 s product-only macro clip.
